posts.title: IG Metall Strikes for a Full Day Against an Offer With No Permanent Raise Until July 2028
posts.description: November 21, 2026 TLDR: More than 150,000 workers at about 100 companies stopped work on November 20, 2026, by IG Metall’s count, in the first full-day strikes in Germany’s metal and electrical industry since 2018. The union wants 5% over one year; employers offer a one-off payment in July 2027 that struggling companies can withhold and a 1.3% raise from July 2028. Strikes continue on Monday, Volkswagen opens its own talks on Tuesday asking for a two-year freeze, and employers in Baden-Württemberg have called talks for Wednesday. More than 150,000 workers at about 100 companies across Germany stopped work for 24 hours on Friday, November 20, IG Metall’s executive said . BMW and Audi plants in Bavaria and the shipyards in the north were among the main sites, and North Rhine-Westphalia had the most companies on strike. It was the first full-day strike in the metal and electrical industry since 2018, in a pay round that covers about 3.7 million workers, Reuters reported , at Mercedes-Benz

posts.title: Korean Battery Makers Fall Behind CATL and BYD Outside China
posts.description: November 18, 2026 TLDR: LG Energy Solution, SK On and Samsung SDI supplied 26.5% of the EV batteries used outside China from January to September 2026, down from 38.2%, SNE Research said on November 4, while CATL and BYD together reached 44.5%. The Korean makers lost the volume in North America, where their usage halved, and some of their US lines are turning to grid storage. China’s two biggest battery makers now supply more of the cells in cars sold outside China than Korea’s three combined. SNE Research’s January to September count , published on November 4, puts CATL and BYD at 44.5% of that market, up 7.8 points. LG Energy Solution, SK On and Samsung SDI fell to 26.5%, from 38.2% a year earlier, when they still led the pair. The market itself grew 24.7%, counting batteries in electric cars, plug-in hybrids and hybrids. North America is where the Korean makers lost the lead, the market their US plants and joint ventures were built to serve. Their combined usage there halved, to 28.

posts.title: Mexico’s Car Output Fell 17.7% in October, Mostly at GM and Stellantis
posts.description: November 18, 2026 TLDR: Mexico’s light-vehicle production fell 17.7% in October 2026 to 302,803, and exports fell 17.9% to 258,137, INEGI’s November 9 report shows. General Motors’ Mexican output nearly halved and Stellantis’s fell 37.4%, together about four-fifths of the drop, while six makers, led by Ford, built more. Mexico’s car plants built 302,803 light vehicles in October, 17.7% fewer than a year earlier, according to the October vehicle report that INEGI, the national statistics institute, published on November 9. Exports fell by a slightly larger share, to 258,137. It is the second double-digit yearly fall in a row: INEGI’s September report had production down 15.1%. Two companies account for most of it. General Motors and Stellantis built about 52,600 fewer vehicles in Mexico than in October 2025, roughly four in five of all the units lost. Without those two, Mexico’s output fell about 5%.
